relationships.subject: CDK5
relationships.evidence_quote: CDK5 may promote NP progression in T2D by increasing the expression of Kalirin-7 and then phosphorylating the NR2B subunit, leading to central sensitization

relationships.subject: Kalirin-7
relationships.evidence_quote: Our previous study suggested that Kalirin-7 can enhance NR2B phosphorylation by PSD95 to facilitate pain behavior [17].

key_findings: Spinal SIRT1 falls in type 2 diabetic neuropathic pain rats; SRT1720 lowers Ac-CDK5, Kalirin-7, p-NR2B and relieves pain.
CDK5 inhibition by roscovitine lowers Kalirin-7 and p-NR2B in vivo and in high-glucose microglia-neuron co-culture.
